rag_summary_count_consistency.details: The five summary labels and their counts agree with the six identified occurrences: Anchoring and insufficient adjustment (1), Availability heuristic (2), Bias blind spot (1), Curse of knowledge (1), and Status quo bias (1).

evaluation_limitations: No retrieved corpus passages or retrieval logs were supplied; corpus fidelity is therefore not scored.
The RAG output is based on retrospective self-report and includes practical constraints that can support legitimate non-bias interpretations.
Only one interview run is evaluated; no dataset-level significance, ranking, or confidence interval is calculated.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: Planning/scoping timeline: “I looked at the 2019 project — six weeks, two staff, reused shell — and treated that as roughly the baseline.”
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The participant anchors the estimate on a smaller prior project and acknowledges only a small adjustment despite known added scope and reduced staffing.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: Scenario format choice: “I went with the legacy template again — third cycle running it. It's the one I know... more comfortable to work in.”
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The participant prefers the repeatedly used legacy format for familiarity and comfort without a formal comparison of training outcomes.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: Severity calibration: “I ended up scaling the peak severity down toward the more familiar flood level” because no comparable flood had occurred locally in forty years.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The participant lets the absence of recent local experience make the modeled catastrophic case feel abstract despite updated risk modeling.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: Peer AAR review: the participant calls a peer's mild scenario a planning gap while saying he was not worried about the same problem in his own concurrent build.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The participant explicitly says he did not apply the same scrutiny to his own concurrent severity reasoning.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: Training inject priority: “Past surveys showed people remember those vividly — I figured that made them the more effective training tool.”
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The participant prioritizes visual injects for memorability over data-rich material carrying the quantitative detail needed for operational decisions.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: Handbook detail: the participant keeps standard shorthand and no glossary because the terms feel standard, despite prior requests for clearer explanations.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The participant treats specialist terminology as obvious to less-experienced partner evaluators.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: Two-week hypothetical: the participant says he would add contingency and split visual/data production more evenly.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: This is a retrospective counterfactual, not an additional hidden occurrence.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: New-planner hypothetical: the participant speculates about different severity scrutiny and handbook assumptions.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: This is a hypothetical comparison and does not add a new decision occurrence.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: Uncertainty close: the participant says the exercise and handbook consequences could have had multiple causes.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The participant reports uncertainty about consequences; no new bias occurrence is asserted.

instance_level_adjudications.hidden_decision_or_episode: Decision point 1: Duration/effort estimation for project scoping
instance_level_adjudications.hidden_mechanism: Designer anchors the new project's timeline estimate on a past, smaller-scope project's completion time, without adjusting for added complexity (three-agency coordination, new hydrology module) or reduced staffing.
instance_level_adjudications.label_equivalence_explanation: The finding uses an established equivalent label: its alternative-label list explicitly includes Planning Fallacy, and the quoted evidence and mechanism match cb_01.
instance_level_adjudications.mechanism_overlap_explanation: The finding directly describes anchoring on the six-week, two-staff prior project and insufficient adjustment for the new module, solo staffing, and three-agency coordination.
instance_level_adjudications.evidence_fidelity_assessment: High fidelity: the quoted participant statements are verbatim and support the reported mechanism.

instance_level_adjudications.hidden_decision_or_episode: Decision point 1: Selection among design-format alternatives
instance_level_adjudications.hidden_mechanism: Designer favors the previously used scenario template/format over a newly recommended modular design, citing comfort/familiarity with the old structure rather than an evidence-based comparison of the two options' training value.
instance_level_adjudications.label_equivalence_explanation: Status quo bias is a related but distinct familiarity-based construct; the finding is correctly localized and its mechanism fits, but Mere Exposure is the hidden target label.
instance_level_adjudications.mechanism_overlap_explanation: The finding directly describes choosing the familiar legacy format without comparative training-outcome evidence.
instance_level_adjudications.evidence_fidelity_assessment: High fidelity: the quoted participant statements are verbatim and support familiarity-driven format selection, while the RAG appropriately notes a legitimate time-saving interpretation.

instance_level_adjudications.hidden_decision_or_episode: Decision point 2: Risk-severity calibration for scenario design based on updated hazard data vs. recent historical experience
instance_level_adjudications.hidden_mechanism: Designer scales back the simulated hazard severity toward the community's recent historical experience (no severe flood in 40 years) despite updated hydrology data showing increased catastrophic risk, treating the absence of recent occurrence as evidence the worst case is unlikely to matter for training purposes.
instance_level_adjudications.label_equivalence_explanation: Availability heuristic is a related but distinct explanation of using readily recalled local history; the finding captures the hidden severity-scaling mechanism but does not use the target Normality Bias label.
instance_level_adjudications.mechanism_overlap_explanation: The finding directly describes scaling down severity because the catastrophic case felt abstract in light of no comparable local event, despite updated modeling.
instance_level_adjudications.evidence_fidelity_assessment: High fidelity: the quoted participant statements are verbatim and support downweighting recent local experience against updated risk modeling; the reported uncertainty is preserved.

instance_level_adjudications.hidden_decision_or_episode: Decision point 2: Self-versus-other evaluation of susceptibility to design distortion during peer AAR review
instance_level_adjudications.hidden_mechanism: While reviewing a peer planner's criticized exercise design in an after-action discussion, the designer attributes the peer's shortcomings to a planning weakness specific to that peer, while expressing confidence that their own concurrent design choices are objective and free of similar influence, without applying the same scrutiny to their own process.
instance_level_adjudications.label_equivalence_explanation: The finding uses the hidden target label and identifies the asymmetric scrutiny of a peer versus the participant own concurrent decision.
instance_level_adjudications.mechanism_overlap_explanation: The finding directly describes criticizing the peer mild scenario while not applying the same scrutiny to the participant own concurrent severity choice.
instance_level_adjudications.evidence_fidelity_assessment: High fidelity: the quoted participant statements are verbatim and explicitly establish the self/other scrutiny asymmetry.

instance_level_adjudications.hidden_decision_or_episode: Decision point 3: Resource allocation among competing training-material formats under time constraint
instance_level_adjudications.hidden_mechanism: Designer allocates the majority of limited remaining production time to photo/video injects on the basis that visual material is more memorable, over data-rich technical injects that carry the specific quantitative information needed for correct operational decisions.
instance_level_adjudications.label_equivalence_explanation: Availability heuristic is a related but distinct vividness-based label; the finding captures prioritizing memorable visual material over operationally relevant data but misses Picture Superiority as the target label.
instance_level_adjudications.mechanism_overlap_explanation: The finding directly describes using vivid recall and impact to prioritize visual injects while underweighting flow-rate information needed for operational decisions.
instance_level_adjudications.evidence_fidelity_assessment: High fidelity: the quoted participant statements are verbatim and support prioritizing memorability over operational decision support.

instance_level_adjudications.hidden_decision_or_episode: Decision point 4: Calibration of explanatory detail for an audience with different background knowledge
instance_level_adjudications.hidden_mechanism: Designer, drawing on 15 years of specialized hydrology/EM background, drafts the Controller-Evaluator handbook using standard practitioner shorthand and acronyms without added explanation, assuming this level of detail is self-evident to all evaluators including those from partner agencies with far less specialized background.
instance_level_adjudications.label_equivalence_explanation: The finding uses the hidden target label and identifies the assumption that specialist shorthand is obvious to less-experienced evaluators.
instance_level_adjudications.mechanism_overlap_explanation: The finding directly describes treating shorthand and scoring conventions as standard despite known differences in partner evaluator background and prior requests for explanation.
instance_level_adjudications.evidence_fidelity_assessment: High fidelity: the quoted participant statements are verbatim and support the audience-calibration failure while acknowledging time pressure.

unmatched_rag_predictions.why_not_an_exact_strict_match: The quote and mechanism match the Mere Exposure instance, but Status quo bias is a near-neighbor label rather than an approved equivalent for the hidden target.
The quote and mechanism match the Normality Bias instance, but Availability heuristic is a related label and is not the approved target label.
The quote and mechanism match the Picture Superiority instance, but Availability heuristic is a related vividness label and is not the approved target label.

high_and_moderate.detection_interpretation: All six positive reasoning segments are detected, and all three negative counterfactual/uncertainty segments are correctly rejected.

rag_label_false_positive_inventory.mechanism_overlap_summary: Full mechanism overlap and exact localization, but the label is not an approved equivalent.
Both occurrences have full mechanism overlap and exact localization, but Availability heuristic is not the approved label for Normality Bias or Picture Superiority.

corpus_support_audit.assessment_note: The RAG explicitly disclosed that no retrieved scientific-paper passages were supplied and provided no corpus citations; this is transparent and does not alter detection or classification scores.

confidence_tradeoff.increment_from_high_to_high_and_moderate: Adding moderate-confidence findings raises segment hit rate from 0.6667 to 1.0000 and strict instance recall from 0.3333 to 0.5000; strict precision remains 0.5000.
confidence_tradeoff.increment_from_high_and_moderate_to_all_: There is no change because all identified findings are already high or moderate confidence.
confidence_tradeoff.increment_from_all_confidence_to_all_con: There is no change because the RAG supplied zero candidate findings.

overall_evaluation_summary.segment_level_primary_result: At the recommended high_and_moderate threshold, all six positive reasoning segments are detected with no false alarms; high_only misses the two moderate-confidence segments.
overall_evaluation_summary.strict_label_plus_mechanism_result: At high_and_moderate, 3 of 6 hidden instances are strict true positives. Three other findings are correctly localized with full mechanisms but use near-neighbor labels, producing strict false positives and false negatives.
overall_evaluation_summary.mechanism_first_result: At high_and_moderate, all six hidden instances are mechanism-first true positives with no false positives because every finding has an exact quote location and full mechanism overlap.
overall_evaluation_summary.candidate_tier_value_assessment: No candidates were supplied, so the candidate-inclusive threshold is identical to the identified-only threshold and provides no additional abstention signal.
main_failure_modes: Three findings use near-neighbor labels instead of the hidden target labels: Status quo bias for Mere Exposure and Availability heuristic for Normality Bias and Picture Superiority.
Moderate-confidence findings are omitted at the high-only threshold.
The RAG ontology choices reduce strict label-plus-mechanism precision despite strong localization and mechanism recovery.
main_strengths: All six identified occurrences are localized to the correct frozen reasoning segments.
All six mechanisms substantially and fully match their hidden instance mechanisms.
The RAG transparently reports that no retrieved corpus support was available and uses verbatim interview evidence.
overall_evaluation_summary.benchmark_interpretation: This run has perfect segment detection and mechanism-first identification at high_and_moderate, but only 0.5000 strict precision, recall, and F1 because three correctly localized mechanisms are expressed with non-approved near-neighbor labels. The result shows a clear taxonomy/label-equivalence gap rather than an evidence-localization or mechanism-recovery failure.
